display.title: The Berditchever's Bag of Sins and the Princess Who Begged Her Father
display.summary_short: Two Yomim Noraim pieces: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev empties the Satan's bag of sins, and the Maggid of Dubno's mashal of a princess explains 'L'shanah haba'ah b'Yerushalayim'.
display.summary_long: The recording begins in the middle of a story of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev (named in the filename) leading the Yomim Noraim davening. At the words 'He acquires His servants in judgment' he suddenly stops, pale and lost in thought, while the whole shul trembles. Later he explains: he saw the Satan's sack of sins left unattended and looked at each sin, and since nearly all had been done by mistake or out of the hardship of golus, they melted away. The furious Satan demanded that he be sold as a slave for theft, but Hashem Himself bought him, as He promised to carry and save His people. Next comes a teaching about the end of Yom Kippur: the shofar after Neilah and the cry 'Next year in Yerushalayim'. The Maggid of Dubno's mashal tells of a king's daughter married to a simple villager. When the king visits, everyone honors her, but she begs him not to leave her behind, and her husband asks the king to raise him to a worthy estate. The storyteller explains: the princess is the Torah, the villagers are the nations, and we ask Hashem to take us out of golus so we can honor His Torah as it deserves.
display.lesson: No Jew is truly bad; most wrongdoing comes from mistakes and hardship, and Hashem redeems His servants. After Yom Kippur we ask Hashem to take us out of golus so we can give the Torah the honor it deserves.
